Bill.BriefDescription: Restoring local control to public schools by repealing the common school code.

BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that the forgottencomponent of the 1993 education reform legislation was that thelegislature was going to provide greater flexibility for schooldistricts and educators. The legislature further finds that thelegislature has made several unsuccessful attempts to whittle away atthe state mandates upon local school districts. The legislatureintends to improve public education in Washington by strengtheninglocal control and repealing the state education code, except to provideeach school board of directors broad, discretionary power to enable SB 6929 p. 6 school districts to be efficient and effective in teaching the publicschool students of Washington state. The legislature further intendsthat all future state laws or rules addressing education be grounded ina philosophy of local control.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to Title 28A RCW toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The board of directors of each school district may exercise thefollowing: (a) The broad discretionary power to determine and adopt writtenpolicies not in conflict with other law that provide for thedevelopment and implementation of programs, activities, services, orpractices that the board determines will: (i) Promote the education and daily physical activity ofkindergarten through twelfth grade students in the public schools; or (ii) Promote the effective, efficient, or safe management andoperation of the school district; (b) Such powers as are expressly authorized by law; and (c) Such powers as are necessarily or fairly implied in the powersexpressly authorized by law. (2) Before adopting a policy under subsection (1)(a) of thissection, the school district board of directors shall comply with thenotice requirements of the open public meetings act, chapter 42.30 RCW,and shall in addition include in that notice a statement that setsforth or reasonably describes the proposed policy. The board ofdirectors shall provide a reasonable opportunity for public written andoral comment and consideration of the comment by the board ofdirectors.

Interested stakeholders are encouraged toinform the legislature as to any additional legislation that needs tobe enacted before December 1, 2010, to enable school districts to beefficient and effective in teaching the public school students ofWashington state when the other statutes are repealed in 2011.
Section 3 of this act takes effect May 1,2011.
